"An Implementation of Integrated Approach in Product Life-Cycle Management Tool to Ensure Requirements-In-Loop During Complex Product Development: A Cubesat Case Study"

RQ1.rationale: Uses RFLP/viewpoints and abstraction for CubeSat system/EPS modeling, but not centered on minimal-knowledge general reference modeling.

RQ2.rationale: Claims traceability, decision support, interoperability, and EPS requirement satisfaction; limited reliability/reproducibility/integrability evidence.

RQ3.rationale: Directly integrates EPS/system requirement parameters with simulation/DOE digital verification before physical development.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: No recurring nanosatellite reference-model lineage is evident from the supplied paper. The method is related to RFLP/3DEXPERIENCE PLM work cited in automotive/aircraft contexts, but the extracted case is a CubeSat electrical-power viewpoint.

study_context_population.mission_platform: Generic CubeSat spacecraft case study in a designated LEO orbit after deployment/detumbling/stabilization.
study_context_population.mission_domain: Electrical-power operation/energy management for a CubeSat; payload/application domain not reported.
study_context_population.organization_type: Research case by authors at Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology; actual mission organization not reported.
study_context_population.project_maturity: Early/conceptual product-development demonstration with digital simulation; no physical/flight maturity reported.

context_evidence.quote: The RFLP approach is implemented using Dassault Systemes 3DExperience platform to simulate a single viewpoint of a Cubesat, focusing on the electrical power view.
The scenario was built in which the Cubesat after releasing into designated orbit had already detumbled and stabilized.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: Assess/use modern PLM tools to maintain requirements traceability and requirements-in-loop during complex/aerospace product development, especially early/conceptual development, using RFLP MBSE.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_and_abstraction: Spacecraft part of a generic CubeSat mission; launch segment excluded. The implemented model is a single electrical-power viewpoint with seven spacecraft subsystems and a global LEO environment; abstraction decreases across RFLP requirements, functional, logical, and physical views.
deliberately_minimal_or_excluded: Only one CubeSat viewpoint/electrical power view simulated
Long-term degradation identified but not shown in the results
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_domain_knowled: Requires stakeholder requirements, numerical requirement thresholds, mission planning/eclipse data, power profile, battery voltage/SoC relationship, subsystem interfaces, and Dymola behavior models. Limited behavior knowledge is handled through viewpoint abstraction and progressive detailing, but the paper does not claim a minimal-domain-knowledge method.

artifact_details.requirements: ENOVIA requirement structure with numerical parameters including voltage, depth-of-discharge/SoC, and SoC >60% threshold.
artifact_details.architecture: SysML functional/logical architecture in CATIA; CubeSat logical system model with subsystems.
artifact_details.behavior_simulation: Dymola behavior models per logical component and whole-system power behavior simulation.
artifact_details.interfaces: Subsystem interfaces defined to transfer data/quantities.
artifact_details.trade_study: DOE matrix with hundreds of configurations modifying battery/EPS parameters.
artifact_details.physical: CAD/physical architecture connected via implement relations.

generality_reuse_mechanism: specific-mission model with reusable method only

key_evidence.quote: Application of MBSE in PLM tool can be performed using an approach called RFLP.
Functional and logical viewpoints are in SysML language and physical aspect of the product developments uses CAD-models.
The requirements are associated with parameters that measure whether the current system configuration satisfies them.

generality_reuse_mechanism_v1_1_reasonin.rationale: The paper presents RFLP-in-PLM as a transferable workflow/method and demonstrates it on one CubeSat electrical-power viewpoint. It discusses abstraction and interfaces, but does not provide or demonstrate a reusable mission-agnostic architecture, template, library, open package, or interface-focused reusable model asset.

evidence.quote: The RFLP approach consists of four methodological stages, represented by its acronym: requirement specification, functional, logical, and physical. These stages are followed sequentially
The RFLP approach is implemented using Dassault Systemes 3DExperience platform to simulate a single viewpoint of a Cubesat, focusing on the electrical power view.
the benefits of the RFLP approach, such as improved requirements traceability, can be fully realized in multiple engineering domains.

toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.toolchain_architecture_data_flow: Requirements and numerical parameters are defined in ENOVIA; CATIA functional/logical engineering reads those parameters and uses them for Dymola behavioral modeling; Dymola behavior models simulate subsystem/system behavior; Assembly/Part Design connects physical architecture to functional/logical architecture through implement relations; DOE explores battery/EPS configurations and requirement conformance.

interoperability_mechanisms.rationale: Explicit internal platform mechanisms are reported, but no codebook-listed exchange format/API/script/import-export mechanism is specified.

toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.syntax_semantic_continuity_evidence: Requirements, functional/logical architecture, Dymola behavior, verification checks, and physical architecture are claimed to be connected in 3DEXPERIENCE; semantic continuity is demonstrated for numerical EPS parameters but not formally validated.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.software_hardware_system_integration_rea: Virtual/system integration of subsystem behavior models is shown; readiness for software/hardware integration, flat-sat, environmental test, or operations is not reported.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.availability_reproducibility: No model files, scripts, DOE matrix data, requirements database, or open packages are reported. Toolchain depends on proprietary 3DEXPERIENCE/CATIA/ENOVIA/Dymola assets.

eps_verification_specific.evidence_integrated_with_model_not_separ: Requirement parameters are appended in ENOVIA, read into CATIA/Dymola behavior modeling, and compared to simulation outputs; the connection web links requirements, behavior, structure, and verification.

evidence.quote: A simulation scenario is created to assess the system's performance against these criteria.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.claim_text_or_paraphrase: Implementing RFLP/MBSE inside 3DEXPERIENCE PLM keeps CubeSat requirements-in-loop and improves requirements traceability in early development.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.artifact_process_linked: ENOVIA requirement structure with numerical parameters linked into CATIA functional/logical architecture and Dymola behavior models via RFLP.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect_size_or_qualitative_effe: Qualitative: authors state that requirements are kept in-loop and traceable; no trace-link counts or baseline are reported.

evidence_source.quote: Requirements are gathered from stakeholder analysis and integrated into the PLM environment to ensure traceability throughout the product development phase.
The implementation of the RFLP approach in Dassault Systemes 3DExperience tool has proven to be highly effective in ensuring requirements-in-loop

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.threats_or_alternative_explanations: Traceability may be a capability of the proprietary PLM environment rather than the RFLP method alone; no quantitative trace coverage or independent assessment is provided.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.reliability_subtype_rationale: Requirements-in-loop and traceability are tied to linking requirements with architectures to provide consistency; this is model/process consistency, not EPS reliability.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.claim_text_or_paraphrase: DOE and linked requirement parameters support timely decision support, change management, and reduced configuration-management complexity during product development.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.artifact_process_linked: Design-of-experiments matrix of configurations modifies battery/EPS parameters and checks conformance against power requirements.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect_size_or_qualitative_effe: Qualitative and procedural: hundreds of configurations are said to be evaluated; no time/effort/configuration-complexity metric is reported.

evidence_source.quote: The product being design is optimized using design of experiments tools which allows to built a web of different configurations and test each of them out to provide decision support
An experiment matrix consisting of hundreds of potential configurations is created to evaluate and identify the optimal battery parameters

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.threats_or_alternative_explanations: The decision-support value is plausible but not measured; the number of configurations is not tied to decision quality, schedule, or avoided rework.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.reliability_subtype_rationale: Decision support, DOE, automation, and configuration-management complexity are not direct reliability claims.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.claim_text_or_paraphrase: The EPS simulation verifies that the selected battery capacity and power management/distribution unit satisfy the SoC requirement and support CubeSat operation over the simulated period.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.artifact_process_linked: Dymola behavior model using eclipse data, power profile, solar-panel production, battery voltage/SoC, PMDU, and SoC acceptance threshold.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect_size_or_qualitative_effe: Reported SoC remains above 90% for 300 minutes against a 60% threshold; battery replenishes to initial value after 300 minutes.

evidence_source.quote: after 300 minutes the battery has replenished to its initial value. It shows that the the Cubesat will have no trouble during its operation. It also verifies that the battery capacity is sufficient and power management unit is working as intended.
the SoC of the battery remained above 90% for a period of 300 minutes, which indicates that the margin is well-suited to satisfy the SoC requirement

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.threats_or_alternative_explanations: Simulation duration is short and no degradation, physical test, or flight validation is reported; results depend on assumed power profile and model fidelity.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.reliability_subtype_rationale: The claim is EPS-specific: simulated battery SoC margin and PMDU behavior are used to argue sufficient operation over the simulated period.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect_size_or_qualitative_effe: Qualitative: comprehensive evaluation is claimed; simulation outputs are shown for the power-view case.

key_findings_by_rq.RQ1: RFLP/viewpoint abstraction can structure a CubeSat system/EPS model across requirements, functional, logical, physical, and behavior domains, but the method is not presented as a minimal-knowledge general reference model.
key_findings_by_rq.RQ2: Claimed outcomes include traceability, consistency, decision support, configuration-management simplification, interoperability/lifecycle continuity, and EPS reliability/mission-assurance proxy via SoC margin. Evidence is strongest for the EPS SoC simulation and weak for broad MBSE process outcomes.
key_findings_by_rq.RQ3: The paper is directly relevant: requirements-in-loop are implemented by linking numerical EPS requirements into Dymola simulations and DOE checks before physical development. The SoC >60% requirement is checked against simulated voltage/SoC over 300 minutes.

synthesis_consistency.notes_for_consistency_with_lineage: Treat as an RFLP/3DEXPERIENCE PLM requirements-in-loop CubeSat power-view case. Do not group with open SysML reference models unless later papers reuse its model; no such reuse is reported here.
synthesis_consistency.confidence_reason: The paper text clearly reports the method, toolchain, and EPS simulation result, but exact venue, mission context, model availability, interface standards, and process-outcome evidence are limited.

repair_notes: Remove over-broad generality coding of interface-focused model unless the main extraction separately justifies it as a reuse mechanism; interfaces are used for simulation/data flow, not shown as reusable model architecture.
Do not add high-level abstraction, mission-agnostic architecture, or low-dynamics / non-detailed-behavior model for this paper.
Keep IVV integration level as simulation-in-the-loop.
Keep EPS reliability limited to the EPS SoC/battery/PMDU claim, not generic requirements traceability or process claims.
